races.name: Racing TV Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up specialist for Tim Easterby with a win on good going over 10f in his most recent start — 11 days between runs is a positive freshness signal, and at 8 years old he knows his job, but needs the pace to collapse to get into it from the back.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sands
runners_data.note: The pivotal horse in this race — front-runner by trade in a field with no other true leader, and her most recent win came over this exact 10f trip on good ground; the [STYLE_FIT] tag signals she is effectively racing into her natural position rather than out of it, making the flag a logical outcome but also her ceiling.

runners_data.name: Sandret
runners_data.note: Prolific winner in form (two wins in last four starts) but a genuine hold-up type whose natural style cannot be executed freely here — mapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded, so Rebecca Hitchen (5lb claim) faces a real positional compromise that will blunt the finishing kick that makes Sandret effective.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 8f on good ground and handles Pontefract-style tracks; Adrian Nicholls sends just one runner in the past 14 days suggesting a focused yard, and Tees George's style of pressing the leader suits this single-pace-setter scenario well.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Consistent on good going with five visits to the frame in her last six runs on that surface, but her true hold-up style is squeezed by the field composition — David Dunsdon will find it hard to get her settled and unleash a meaningful late run if the pace is controlled and the field races compactly.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: 51 days off the track is the longest absence in this field and a mild freshness query; she has bumped into traffic in two of her last three but her prominent racing style makes her one of the logical passengers just off Shimmering Sands, and Ruth Carr's 3/33 recent strike-rate is respectable.

runners_data.name: Ephron
runners_data.note: The only 3-year-old in the field with a recent win on good ground over 8f — youth and freshness on a flat track could be an asset, and Amy Collier holds the mount; a hold-up type whose course in this race depends heavily on the leaders setting a strong enough gallop.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at 9 and the lowest-rated (OR 50), fitted with tongue-strap and visor; a genuine hold-up horse who faces the same overcrowding problem at the rear, and with a [STYLE_FIT] discount and Evie Lee taking 7lbs off a modest weight, the profile here is of a horse racing against the grain of the pace shape.

races.paceDynamic: Shimmering Sands is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f Pontefract handicap and, with no other natural leader to challenge for the early lead, she will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good ground. Tees George and Star Start are the prominent types most likely to sit directly behind her, forming a compact early group, while the genuine hold-up horses — Yermanthere, Ephron — will settle further back. The field carries a significant cluster of horses tagged as true hold-up types (Sandret, Princess Niyla, Wrist Art) who are redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed; in practice, the race shape behind Shimmering Sands will be condensed rather than strung out, limiting the advantage of a deep hold-up position. With one uncontested pace-setter setting a measured tempo on a flat course, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Shimmering Sands economically and pounce approaching the home straight, rather than closers who need a searching gallop to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shimmering Sands Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Shimmering Sands secures an uncontested lead and sets a measured, confidence-building tempo that is never seriously quickened by rivals.
scenarios.body: If Shimmering Sands secures an uncontested lead and sets a measured, confidence-building tempo that is never seriously quickened by rivals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Tees George or Star Start track Shimmering Sands closely enough to pounce as she ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Tees George or Star Start track Shimmering Sands closely enough to pounce as she ties up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Finds Best Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses sharply in the final two furlongs and the compressed midfield bunch generates a late surge.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses sharply in the final two furlongs and the compressed midfield bunch generates a late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scrambled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Shimmering Sands sets a falsely slow early tempo and then is swamped by multiple rivals simultaneously in a compressed sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If Shimmering Sands sets a falsely slow early tempo and then is swamped by multiple rivals simultaneously in a compressed sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Shimmering Sands is the fulcrum of this race — if she gets uncontested to the front and Mr Henry Callan settles her cleanly, the entire field is at her mercy, but if she is taken on early by Tees George for the prominent berth the race shape changes entirely.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Sandret, Princess Niyla, Wrist Art) will all be hunting the same late ground — watch for traffic and interference in the final two furlongs as they attempt to navigate around a compact midfield pack.

Tees George has a headgear note (no headgear) and has placed at Pontefract-profile tracks before — watch whether Mr Jack Lander (5lb) sends him forward to press Shimmering Sands or elects to stalk, as that decision will define whether Scenario A or B unfolds.

Star Start has been off 51 days — watch her in the preliminaries and early stages; if she shows any sign of race-rustiness, her prominent position becomes a liability rather than an asset in a pace-dependent race like this.

Ephron as the sole 3-year-old carries a developmental wildcard — watch whether Miss Amy Collier rides her hold-up or angles forward, as a confident prominent ride on a horse with recent good-ground winning form could surprise the older, higher-rated rivals.

races.name: Danny O'Neill Birthday 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Napoleons Casino Bradford Handicap

runners_data.name: Sir Paul Ramsey
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston has the in-form yard angle (6/44 T14) and Jason Hart rides a genuine hold-up horse whose Good-ground figures (9/15 similar going) are solid, though 61 days off the track and a tendency to finish late makes him vulnerable in what is likely to be a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Dovey Moon
runners_data.note: The race pivot — David Evans' four-year-old has won twice on Good ground at this trip and PJ McDonald is aboard; her STYLE_FIT flag matters only if something pushes her off the front, which looks unlikely given the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Kaleido
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's prominent runner won over 7f on Good ground and Tudhope is a shrewd pilot in tactical races; has finished mid-pack in recent 1m Good-ground starts so needs to improve, but suits the likely shape tracking just off the leader.

runners_data.name: Selection
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's four-year-old has placed twice in similar conditions and the headgear (p) suggests a horse who needs organising, but a prominent style suits this controlled tempo and David Nolan's experience in handicaps is a positive.

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 11-year-old has solid Good-ground form (3W6P in similar conditions, 11/15 similar going) but is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map; at 14 days since last run he is fit, yet his true off-pace style is compromised by the lack of a strong gallop.

runners_data.name: Sunriseontheboyne
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's hold-up runner has produced nothing better than eighth in recent Good-ground starts and lacks the striking form needed to make an impression at Pontefract; Andrew Mullen picks up the ride but the horse's overall profile is weak in this field.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Sam England's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose best form is over longer trips (10f+), and at 1m with a solo front runner to track, he is effectively racing out of his preferred position and distance sweet-spot, limiting his winning prospects despite a reasonable T14 strike rate (4/11).

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: David O'Meara saddles this eight-year-old with Mark Winn, and although the horse prefers to race prominently, the crowded position market means he is unlikely to slot in where he wants; his form on Good ground at this trip reads 5,9,10 recently, and age and recent finishing positions suggest he is struggling at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Dovey Moon is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine pace rivals looking to push for the lead from the outset, PJ McDonald should be able to dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front on the 1m Pontefract circuit. Good ground suits the entire field and a sustainable gallop is the most likely outcome, meaning the race will be run to suit horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs. This race shape favours prominent or close-tracking runners who can be delivered with a smooth challenge once Dovey Moon kicks for home, rather than deep hold-up horses who need a stronger pace to close into. The field carries more prominent and hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate — Jez Bomb, Cosmos Raj and Garden Oasis are genuine prominent or hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their natural position in what will be a relatively slowly-run, strung-out affair led by a single front runner, reducing their expected influence.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dovey Moon Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dovey Moon is allowed to stride clear uncontested and sets a measured, controlled pace that suits her strengths.
scenarios.body: If Dovey Moon is allowed to stride clear uncontested and sets a measured, controlled pace that suits her strengths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overtakes
scenarios.trigger: If a close-tracking prominent racer travels comfortably into the race and produces a decisive late challenge to overhaul Dovey Moon.
scenarios.body: If a close-tracking prominent racer travels comfortably into the race and produces a decisive late challenge to overhaul Dovey Moon.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and genuine hold-up horses get the strong gallop they need to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than expected and genuine hold-up horses get the strong gallop they need to close from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace causes the field to bunch entering the final two furlongs and the race becomes a sprint finish with positional chaos.
scenarios.body: If the slow pace causes the field to bunch entering the final two furlongs and the race becomes a sprint finish with positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Dovey Moon is the sole front runner — watch whether PJ McDonald is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first two furlongs, because an uncontested lead on Good ground massively increases her chance of lasting home.

Selection carries headgear (p) and prominent runners are plentiful in this field — watch whether David Nolan can slot her into an early, comfortable berth just off Dovey Moon, as getting shuffled back would undermine her chance entirely.

Jez Bomb and Cosmos Raj are both natural prominent types who may jostle for position in the early stages — a minor scrimmage for the prominent berths could compromise both their races and inadvertently benefit the front runner by any brief pace surge settling back down.

Sir Paul Ramsey is 61 days off the track for the in-form Charlie Johnston yard — watch his market move as a stable that fires on 6/44 runners in 14 days often knows when a horse is ready, and if he drifts it may confirm the hold-up draw is too big an ask here.

Garden Oasis, at 11 years old with recent Good-ground place form, is a runner to monitor for market support — Tim Easterby frequently places horses to best effect, but the steady pace is a real threat to his hold-up style regardless of fitness.

races.name: Pontefract Ladies Day Wednesday 5th August Handicap

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Two course-and-distance wins on good ground and a clear record of front-running at Pontefract give Ruth Carr's six-year-old the ideal profile here; James Sullivan rides and the combination can dictate entirely unopposed — style fit of 0.93 suggests some minor positional risk but she is the natural leader of this field.

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's six-year-old has run respectable races in similar good-ground sprints and returns after only 13 days; a natural hold-up horse who will be racing further forward than ideal because the field is saturated with closers, which may not suit his finishing style in a race that could be run at a muddling tempo.

runners_data.name: Queen Sana
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's lightly-raced three-year-old has an impressive sequence of placed efforts — four seconds in her last five runs — on good and firm ground at 5-6f, and Daniel Tudhope is a booking that commands respect; she is a genuine hold-up type whose consistent form at this level makes her the most reliable closer if Betweenthesticks does tire.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground last time out and Tim Easterby's seven-year-old carries a tongue-tie as he tends to; David Allan is an experienced northern pilot, but this horse's true hold-up style means he needs a strong gallop to close into — a controlled solo pace from Betweenthesticks is not his friend despite that recent win.

runners_data.name: Knicks
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides the five-year-old for Michael & David Easterby; four placed efforts in recent runs suggest consistency but no win on good ground, and being squeezed from her natural rear position into a midfield role where she cannot find clear daylight is a genuine tactical problem in a compressed sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Soca Star
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's three-year-old has been placed twice on good ground at 5f and goes on 35 days' absence; Dale Swift takes the ride and this filly has enough early pace to press Betweenthesticks if ridden prominently, making her one of the more dangerous hold-up types if she is actually ridden to take a closer pitch.

runners_data.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground at a recent start and Kevin Ryan's four-year-old wears a hood; Jack Nicholls claims 5lb which brings his weight down to a competitive 132lbs, and his best form is on softer surfaces — five of his fifteen runs on similar ground have produced only one win, so the good ground is a mild question mark despite that recent victory.

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: Tina Jackson's five-year-old has been placed three times in her last five runs on good ground at 5-6f and Jason Hart knows the northern sprint scene well; occupying a midfield slot on the map while being a natural finisher from off the pace, she needs a pace collapse rather than a controlled Betweenthesticks gallop to get competitive and her OR of 57 is the field's lowest.

races.paceDynamic: Betweenthesticks is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Pontefract handicap and, with no other genuine pace horse to push her along, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset — Ruth Carr's mare has won twice at this track and trip on good ground and will not be pressured into going too fast. The remaining seven runners are all hold-up or midfield types by nature, meaning the bulk of the field will be tracking a single pace-setter rather than racing against each other for the lead, which tightens the race into a straight-line chase from the halfway mark. Five of those hold-up horses have been redistributed into midfield on the pace map simply because there are not enough rear positions to accommodate them all, so the finishing straight at Pontefract — which is demanding and uphill — will see a wall of closers arriving together behind Betweenthesticks. This race shape decisively favours a horse that can sit just off the controlled pace in a prominent position and pick off a front-runner who has had things her own way, making the second or third horse out of the bend — effectively the Prominent-to-Lead profile — the sweet spot; true deep closers face a high risk that Betweenthesticks simply never hits a wall.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Betweenthesticks Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Betweenthesticks secures the lead unopposed and sets a controlled, measured tempo that the closers simply cannot reel in up the Pontefract climb.
scenarios.body: If Betweenthesticks secures the lead unopposed and sets a controlled, measured tempo that the closers simply cannot reel in up the Pontefract climb.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Chargers Swamp Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Betweenthesticks goes slightly too quick in her solo role and ties up inside the final furlong, allowing the best-rated closers to mow her down.
scenarios.body: If Betweenthesticks goes slightly too quick in her solo role and ties up inside the final furlong, allowing the best-rated closers to mow her down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffle Produces Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the tightly bunched group of redistributed hold-up types all travel smoothly and deliver simultaneously, creating a multi-horse photo at the line.
scenarios.body: If the tightly bunched group of redistributed hold-up types all travel smoothly and deliver simultaneously, creating a multi-horse photo at the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Raider Steals March
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling prominently — Queen Sana or Soca Star — presses Betweenthesticks much earlier than expected, forcing a two-horse duel that burns off the pure closers.
scenarios.body: If a horse travelling prominently — Queen Sana or Soca Star — presses Betweenthesticks much earlier than expected, forcing a two-horse duel that burns off the pure closers.

watchPoints.text: Betweenthesticks has sole control of the gallop — watch whether James Sullivan elects to roll along at a true pace or dawdles, because if she crawls the final furlong climb could see the entire chasing pack engulf her simultaneously.

Queen Sana has finished second four times in recent starts; watch whether Daniel Tudhope positions her much closer to the pace than her hold-up tag suggests, as doing so could transform her from a consistent placer into a winner.

Dream Deal won last time on good ground at 5f but is a genuine hold-up type being mapped to midfield — watch for David Allan dropping him in behind rather than tracking in the middle, as a truly run race is the only shape that brings him into contention.

Lucius Aurelius carries the 5lb claimer Jack Nicholls — watch for any signs in the early stages that the hood is helping him settle, as his recent form is on softer ground and a drop in class here could see him outrun his odds if the pace is honest.

Five of the eight runners have been active within the last 13-18 days — watch the market move on any of Hover On The Wind, Dream Deal or Knicks in the final hour, as trainer form for Midgley (T14: 2/19) and Tim Easterby (5/91) suggests runners in form rather than off a prep.

races.name: Wilfred Underwood Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's hold-up runner has shown consistent form over this 6f trip on Good ground (placed at 6f/Good twice in last five), and with 11 days since last run is fresh enough; sits at the rear naturally and needs a clear passage late — traffic in this compressed field is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Profiled as a hold-up horse but redistributed to the lead as the sole pace-setter; races 8 days after its last run, and while the Good ground suits, it is operating out of its natural style at a STYLE_FIT of 0.80 — sustainable pace is likely but its overall chance is tempered by the role reversal.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Fahey's three-year-old has the highest similar-going placing (4/6 on Good) of the deep closers, though form figures of 84-005 reflect inconsistency; at 14 days since last run Oisin Orr's booking is an upgrade, and this horse needs a strong pace to lay siege from the back.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: Veteran seven-year-old who has been running primarily over 5f on Good — now stepping up to 6f — and while true instincts are as a hold-up type, it sits shown in midfield due to field compression (STYLE_FIT=0.92); tongue-tie noted, and its 5f form over Good is competitive but the extra furlong is a genuine query.

runners_data.name: Full Gas
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping; 42 days off the track is the longest absence in the field, and while the 2nd at 6f/Good is the standout relevant form, the layoff and racing forward of its natural position (STYLE_FIT=0.91) introduces doubt.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' three-year-old has a form string built almost entirely over 7f on Soft or Standard, making this step back to 6f on Good a notable profile shift; though mapped to midfield, its natural style is hold-up and its best finishing positions have come at longer trips where it can sustain its run.

runners_data.name: Lady Bouquet
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old has good recent 5f form on Good but steps up to 6f here — a trip it has run at before without winning — and is mapped into midfield having been profiled as a hold-up type; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a small positive but the step in trip against an already awkward positional scenario is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Easterby's three-year-old is the youngest and lowest-rated runner, yet holds a recent win at 6f on Good and has course-type familiarity; Lewis Chalkley's 7lb claim helps at the weights, but it is shown in midfield out of its natural rearward position (STYLE_FIT=0.91) and will need to be streetwise in a compressed field.

races.paceDynamic: Ideal Guest is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this field, redistributed to the front having been profiled as a hold-up type, meaning the race will likely be run at a sustainable, controlled tempo rather than a truly contested gallop — a lone, unharried leader dictating on their own terms over Pontefract's 6f on Good ground. Behind, the bulk of the field — Full Gas, Superstorm, Kyber Crystal, Lady Bouquet, and Ganthorpe — are genuine hold-up or prominent types compressed into midfield because there is simply no room for all of them to settle in their natural position. Big Apple Jack and Great Success are the truest hold-up operators and will be furthest back, relying on a strong late sectional that a slow-to-moderate pace may not generate. The race shape strongly favours a hold-up runner who can produce a sustained finish, but the compressed, traffic-heavy midfield creates meaningful risk — the real beneficiaries are those able to travel smoothly and quicken off a measured gallop, meaning a runner capable of sitting just off the pace and finding a clear passage is best placed, rather than a deep closer who needs a strongly-run race to get into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ideal Guest Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Ideal Guest sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the midfield compression creates a messy cavalry charge that stalls closers.
scenarios.body: If Ideal Guest sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the midfield compression creates a messy cavalry charge that stalls closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to stretch the field and a hold-up runner secures a clear passage to deliver a telling late challenge.
scenarios.body: If the pace is honest enough to stretch the field and a hold-up runner secures a clear passage to deliver a telling late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow it compresses the entire field into a sprint finish and a horse tracking midfield strikes from a prominent but uncontested position.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so slow it compresses the entire field into a sprint finish and a horse tracking midfield strikes from a prominent but uncontested position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Ideal Guest sets an unexpectedly fierce early pace and ties up, gifting a late-finishing hold-up horse the spoils in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Ideal Guest sets an unexpectedly fierce early pace and ties up, gifting a late-finishing hold-up horse the spoils in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Ideal Guest racing as a reluctant front-runner out of role — if it jumps slowly or is headed briefly at any point, there is no natural backup pace-setter and the race could collapse into a messy sprint finish with unpredictable results.

Big Apple Jack and Great Success are the deepest closers in the field — watch for both being caught in traffic through the first four furlongs as the bunched midfield leaves little room to manoeuvre on Pontefract's turning track.

Full Gas returns from a 42-day absence in a race where it cannot get its natural hold-up position — a fresh horse operating forward of its preferred berth is an unknown quantity and could either unsettle others or fade tamely from the front half of the field.

Kyber Crystal's move from 5f to 6f on Good is untested in recent form — if the extra furlong finds it out, it will drop away through the final furlong and could cause interference to those making ground from the rear.

Ganthorpe's recent 6f win on Good is the most directly relevant piece of form in the field — watch whether Lewis Chalkley positions it aggressively early to exploit that course fitness before the hold-up pack can organise their challenges.

races.name: Wayne Conway Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Anificas Beauty
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over this exact course and distance on Good ground make her immediately relevant; a natural hold-up horse who has shown she can travel close enough here to strike, and 13 days since last run is ideal freshness.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with Ruth Carr showing 1 winner from 27 runners in the last 14 days — modest form — but Good ground and 8f suits her best, and Joanna Mason's patient hold-up style is at least authentic to the horse's natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Gained his win over 10f on Tapeta and his Good-ground record over today's trip is limited; a genuine hold-up operator whose true style is displaced here into midfield, meaning Jason Hart will need to manufacture a run from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Nakatomi
runners_data.note: The headgear notation and 23 days absence are minor flags; at heart a closer whose best effort this season came second over today's trip on Good, but Tom Eaves will find the horse operating further forward than it wants, blunting the late run.

runners_data.name: Far Ahead
runners_data.note: Back-to-back runner-up finishes on Good and Soft over this trip signal strong each-way claims, and Oisin Orr's record with the Fahey yard is a positive; naturally a hold-up horse pushed closer to the pace than ideal, but the talent in form is genuine.

runners_data.name: Shark Two One
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the pivot of this entire race; goes on Good ground, has placed form at 7f and is stepping up a furlong which could help him settle; headgear (p) noted, and the amateur 5lb claimer Ethan Tindall will need to judge the fractions carefully to preserve the advantage.

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: John Wainwright's stable in fair nick (3/7 in 14 days) and Paul Mulrennan is a strong jockey booking; at seven years old she carries headgear and her runs on Good at 8f are consistent without threatening — her role in midfield here is forced upon her rather than chosen.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: Three-year-old in excellent recent form with a win and two places at 8f on Good ground; P J McDonald takes over and this horse's CV — including that Good-ground win — fits today's conditions precisely, making her the most naturally suited horse behind the pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Captain Bruce
runners_data.note: The ⚠ finish-fade flag is significant — this horse's last five runs show a pattern of weakening, and the 32-day absence plus no wins on Good or firm and poor Pontefract sim-going marks it as the most vulnerable runner in the field; Cam Hardie faces an uphill task.

races.paceDynamic: Shark Two One is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — the remainder of the field is stacked with hold-up types who will be content to track rather than challenge for the lead. Pontefract's one-mile trip is a horseshoe circuit with a long run-in, meaning a well-judged front-running display at a sustainable gallop can absolutely be preserved to the line, particularly on Good ground where Shark Two One's going profile reads fine. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate in their natural roles: Daring Leader, Nakatomi, Far Ahead, Elettaria, and Captain Bruce are all genuine closers who will be forced closer to the pace than they would prefer, compromising their ability to deliver the sweeping late run their style demands. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone, uncontested pace-setter on a fair surface with no serious mid-race pressure favours horses that can race prominently or just off the early gallop and sustain their effort — pure closers operating out of position are at a structural disadvantage in this shape.

scenarios.title: Shark Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Shark Two One bowls along at a comfortable solo clip and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: If Shark Two One bowls along at a comfortable solo clip and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Alice's Influence or Anificas Beauty track Shark Two One closely and pick him off in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Alice's Influence or Anificas Beauty track Shark Two One closely and pick him off in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely honest enough to soften Shark Two One and the redistributed hold-up types arrive from further back.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is genuinely honest enough to soften Shark Two One and the redistributed hold-up types arrive from further back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Shark Two One is challenged early by horses unwilling to settle and the race develops into a ragged affair with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: If Shark Two One is challenged early by horses unwilling to settle and the race develops into a ragged affair with no clear beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Shark Two One's lead is the race — watch whether Ethan Tindall (5lb claimer) controls the fractions sensibly or allows the tempo to drift so slowly that the hold-up horses arrive with a rush in the final 2f.

Alice's Influence is the most dangerous closer to the front-runner given her recent back-to-back Good-ground placements at 8f; watch P J McDonald's positioning in the first 3f — if he tracks Shark immediately, the race opens up.

Far Ahead's two consecutive second-place finishes over this trip suggest a horse in good heart despite being pushed out of its natural hold-up role; monitor whether Oisin Orr can manufacture a clear run from the middle of the pack.

Captain Bruce's finish-fade warning and 32-day layoff combined with zero wins on comparable ground make it a live danger to those around it in-running — watch for it weakening and causing interference at a crucial stage of the race.

Nakatomi wears a hood and has had 23 days off; if the horse is fractious or fails to settle into a forced midfield position, it could disrupt the running of nearby rivals including Daring Leader and Far Ahead who are also out of their natural roles.
